title: Hagelloch 1861: the Pink Book's periods, the prodrome from Pfeilsticker

source.citation: CDC. Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (the Pink Book), chapter 13: Measles. Page dated 24 April 2024.

evidence.quote: The time from exposure to rash onset averages 14 days
evidence.working: 14 days from exposure to the rash, less the 4 days a person transmits before it: 10 days infected and not yet infectious, on average. The chapter gives averages only; no spread is assumed here, so every child takes 10.

source.citation: Pfeilsticker A. Beiträge zur Pathologie der Masern mit besonderer Berücksichtigung der statistischen Verhältnisse. Tübingen: Eberhard-Karls-Universität; 1863.
source.read: OCR text of the incubation chapter, 2026-11-18

evidence.quote: dass die Zeit von der Ansteckung bis zur Eruption … constant 14 Tage sei (that the time from infection to the rash is a constant 14 days)
evidence.working: Pfeilsticker upholds Panum's rule, quoting him: the first symptoms come usually 10 to 12 days after infection, the rash on the 14th. The 10 days of the latent period, taken from the Pink Book, leave 4 days of prodrome before the rash. He reports the rash-to-rash interval in a household as usually 10 or 11 days, not 14, because a child infects others before its own rash: the prodrome transmits.
evidence.note: Aaby, Thoma and Dietz (2022, J Infect 84:668–674, closed) give a mean prodrome of 3.8 days for children Pfeilsticker saw and 4.2 for those recalled. Every child takes 4 here.

source.citation: CDC. Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (the Pink Book), chapter 13: Measles. Page dated 24 April 2024.

evidence.quote: transmissible from 4 days before through 4 days after rash onset
evidence.working: The day of the rash and the 4 days after it: 5 days. With the 4-day prodrome, 9 infectious days in all, as in the Pink Book set.

evidence.note: The spike's assumption; to be fitted to the 1861 curve. The chapter's secondary attack rate of more than 90% among susceptible close contacts would need at least 0.23 a day over 9 days; a Hagelloch household is not the same setting.
